title: Choose the visual world for the GTMagic chat
question: The roll assigned the Departure Board. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Departure Board
options.thesis: A run is a timetable and the crowd is the board: every customer is a flap that clatters onto the message they chose.
options.viewport: Light chat thread on the left at reading width; a dark flap board docks right, 48 cells flipping to A–F or a dash for none, with the tally rows beneath.
options.risk: A retro-station trope if the board turns into decoration rather than the live count.

raised.raise: Focusing a flap dims the board and opens that customer's card with their real quotes.
No bubble chrome around messages: the type scale alone carries who is speaking.
Every message and customer keeps one fixed code (A–F, C-01…C-48) used identically in chat, board and report.
Sources hang as margin keys beside each finding instead of footnotes.
All counts in tabular numerals, n always printed beside the count.

options.label: Isotype Count
options.thesis: One figure is one customer: the answer is a picture-statistic you can count by eye.
options.viewport: Chat thread centered; results arrive as plates of repeated figures in rows per message, coloured by customer group.
options.risk: Familiar infographic territory; pictograms can read cute instead of rigorous.

options.label: Ticket Wallet
options.thesis: Each pipeline step is a coupon that stamps itself done; honesty labels are literal stamps.
options.viewport: Chat thread as a stack of coupons; results arrive on a fare-box coupon with SIMULATED stamped across the counts.
options.case: Fuses well on product clarity (stamps make SIMULATED and DRAFT unmissable); loses on audience identification.
options.risk: Travel nostalgia owners don't connect to their market problem.

options.label: Streaming Wall
options.thesis: Results as rows of tiles that expand on focus.
options.viewport: Rows of message tiles; the focused one grows.
options.case: Loses both axes: browsing entertainment, not deciding who to sell to.
options.kept: Focus expands one item while the rest dims.

options.label: Metro Tiles
options.thesis: Giant lowercase type and flat colour tiles as the interface.
options.viewport: Panorama of tiles with cropped headings.
options.case: Loses both axes: a dated OS costume with no tie to the owner's world.
options.kept: Chrome deleted; type alone carries hierarchy.

options.label: Catalog Sleeve
options.thesis: Everything numbered, names replaced by codes.
options.viewport: A pulse plot of responses on black.
options.case: Loses both axes: deliberate obscurity fights plain answers.
options.kept: One fixed catalog code per item, used everywhere.

options.label: Centre-Rail Edition
options.thesis: Twin columns around a keyed rail, apparatus in the margin.
options.viewport: Findings in two columns with sources in the margin.
options.case: Loses both axes: scholarly, slow, and a chat cannot be twin columns.
options.kept: Sources hang in the margin beside the claim.

options.label: Datamatics
options.case: Loses both axes: strobing art installation, unreadable for an owner.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A familiar AI chat app, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar, centered thread, composer at the bottom; results as cards in the thread.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other chat wrapper by design.
